explanations: Robert Hooke examined it microscopically, and that led to his discovery and naming of the cell.
The montado landscape of Portugal produces roughly half of the world's annual harvest.
It is made up of suberin, a hydrophobic substance, at about 40%, with lignin next at 22%.
It is the phellem layer of bark, harvested mainly from Quercus suber, native to southwest Europe and northwest Africa.
Being impermeable, buoyant, elastic and fire retardant, its commonest product is the wine stopper.

sources.excerpt: Cork was examined microscopically by Robert Hooke, which led to his discovery and naming of the cell.
The montado landscape of Portugal produces approximately half of the cork harvested annually worldwide, with Corticeira Amorim being the leading company in the industry.
Cork is composed of suberin, a hydrophobic substance.
However, in general, cork is made up of suberin (average of about 40%), lignin (22%), polysaccharides (cellulose and hemicellulose) (18%), extractables (15%) and others.
It is the phellem layer of bark tissue which is harvested for commercial use primarily from Quercus suber (the cork oak), which is native to southwest Europe and northwest Africa.
Because of its impermeable, buoyant, elastic, and fire retardant properties, it is used in a variety of products, the most common of which is wine stoppers.
